To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

microparticles, which are released from different cells, can modulate the formation of new blood vessels in vitro and in vivo by acting directly on endothelial cells and/or indirectly through the modulation of soluble factors and/or progenitor cells.
microparticles are emerging as a new therapeutic tool for the modulation of angiogenesis.
microparticles are a new therapeutic tool for angiogenesis and vascular remodeling.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel class of materials, the so-called microparticles, for the treatment of cardiovascular disease.
the development of new therapeutic approaches for the treatment of cardiovascular disease, in particular, atherosclerosis and restenosis, by using microparticles as therapeutic tools.
the development of new strategies to prevent or cure cardiovascular disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the term “vasculogenesis” is not synonymous with “angiogenesis” and the term “neovascularization” is not synonymous either with “vasculogenesis,” or “angiogenesis” or both.
microparticles are involved in angiogenesis and vasculogenesis, and their effects are dependent on the origin of the microparticles.
microparticles are a heterogeneous population of vesicles that are released by cells under normal and pathological conditions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
microparticles are not only biomarkers but also vectors of biological information.
microparticles are not just “cell dust” anymore, but are true biomarkers and therapeutic tools.
we have identified a new mechanism for the regulation of vascular development, and that we have shown that this mechanism can be exploited for the therapeutic treatment of vascular diseases.

the endothelial microparticles can be used to promote neovascularization in vivo.
the use of microparticles as therapeutic tools in angiogenesis-associated diseases should be considered in a context of personalized medicine.
